answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the zenith seed, the echo timing is verifiable from the harbor record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 243 keys thus pays 243 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 173 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. That is 18 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
